title: Make the operators of exudyn.symbolic agree with numpy: * of two vectors or with a matrix refused, multiply, numpy ufuncs
author: Claude-JG
description: The operator * of two symbolic vectors is their scalar product, of matrices and of a matrix and a vector the matrix product; numpy multiplies the components. * of vectors and matrices raises a TypeError that names dot(), @ and multiply(); exudyn.special.deprecations.symbolicStarProduct restores the old meaning for the transition. Vector.multiply is the product of the components. Numpy's ufuncs (np.multiply, np.sin, np.sqrt, np.arctan2, np.maximum, a numpy array times or plus a symbolic vector) compute with symbolic operands instead of refusing them. Indexing raises IndexError and takes negative indices, so that a symbolic vector is a sequence; a vector divided by a scalar, 2**x and abs(x) are added. The comparison with numpy in python is a test.
releaseNotes: The operators of exudyn.symbolic mean what they mean for numpy, so that one user function computes with numpy arrays and records with symbolic vectors: * of two symbolic vectors, of two matrices or of a matrix and a vector raises a TypeError (numpy multiplies the components; use @, dot() or multiply()), as does == of two vectors; exudyn.special.deprecations.symbolicStarProduct = True restores the scalar and matrix products for the transition. New: Vector.multiply, numpy's functions with symbolic operands (np.multiply, np.dot, np.sin, np.sqrt, np.arctan2, np.maximum, a numpy array plus or times a symbolic vector), a vector divided by a scalar, 2**x, abs(x), v[-1], sum(v); CreateSymbolicUserFunction records q and q_t of the bodies and systems with their size. Test model symbolicNumpyCompatibilityTest.py.
